newsitem.title: UK: British report on abattoir dangers "suppressed"-FT.
newsitem.headline: British report on abattoir dangers "suppressed"-FT.

text.p: The British government has been called on by the opposition to explain why a report which revealed shortcomings in hygiene standards at abattoirs was not published, the Financial Times said on Thursday.

It said the report, carried out by government hygiene inspectors, exposed lapses in hygiene in some abattoirs and warned of "major contamination" of carcases by animal faeces, which harbour the deadly bacteria E coli.
The Financial Times said the report was due to be published in March last year, but a decision was taken not to go ahead.
The Ministry of Agriculture told the paper the report was an internal document and a spokesman said ministers had not seen it at any stage.
An outbreak of food poisoning caused by the O157 strain of E coli in Scotland late last year has so far claimed 17 victims and more than 400 victims have been treated for confirmed E coli poisoning.

"If the recommendations in the report were being implemented uniformly and fully across the country, the risk from E coli O157 would be considerably diminished," the FT quoted Bill Swain, editor of the report, as saying.
The FT said opposition Labour called on the government to make a statement in the House of Commons to explain its actions.
